newsitem.title: USA: Prudential to pay Texas $2 million to settle case.
newsitem.headline: Prudential to pay Texas $2 million to settle case.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co of America agreed to pay a $2 million fine and improve its restitution offer to victims of alleged deceptive sales practices, Texas Insurance Commissioner Elton Bomer said.
Prudential entered into the agreement in principle without admitting wrongdoing or violations of Texas consumer protection laws.
The fine will go into the state's general revenue fund, Bomer said.
It is almost three times the $700,000 that Prudential earlier offered to pay last summer following a nationwide investigation coordinated by the New Jersey insurance commissioner.
Under a class-action settlement reached in September, Prudential agreed to pay at least $410 million to as many as 10.7 million policyholders.
Texas, as well as Florida, California and Massachusetts objected to that class-action settlement.
Under Thursday's agreement, Bomer will withdraw his objection to the class-action settlement, the Texas Department of Insurance said.
The class-action settlement and Bomer's agreement with Prudential affect about 250,000 Texans who bought Prudential permanent life insurance policies between 1982 and 1995.
Total Texas restitution is estimated at $25 million, the insurance department said.
Financial experts estimate that restitution will average about $2,500 per claimant, the department said. Individual relief will vary according to the facts.
The agreement will make it easier for consumers to prove they were deceived and enables people who were 60 or older at the time of the alleged deception to get the maximum amount of relief available.
